paragraphs.source_en: Considering the visibility and the navigation, it is evident that the character of some painted sites is open, such as those located in wadies or on a hill with painted walls exposed to the exterior and perceptible from a distance. In these cases the paintings were revealed to everyone who passed nearby; in the wadies there was no choice as the shelters were the only available place to paint. However, in the stone cities the external position of the paintings is clearly intentional, particularly if there are suitable but empty shelters also in the internal parts. On the contrary, the character of paintings inside the labyrinth of corridors is evidently hidden. In the Tassili where the variety of sites is greater, both open and hidden painted sites are found.

paragraphs.source_en: Ample, long and high walls often present large Round Head compositions but such walls may also present only small-sized images. Some shelters have very low roofs, so that the painter had to be sitting or lying on the floor when painting. In these cases the images are usually not visible from outside, so they can be considered hidden, especially where there are other suitable but empty walls nearby. Paintings are often located around large natural holes in the wall, called arches and isolated rock formations were also chosen for image-making. Images were usually placed on the central part of the wall but they also occur near the ground or in such elevated positions that reaching them from the floor is impossible.
